Fit the model at several classifier thresholds

Source: R/fp_threshold_sweep.R
fp_threshold_sweep.Rd

The threshold at which a confidence score counts as a detection trades false positives against missed detections, and it can change the estimated environmental effects (Piatti et al. 2026). This function builds the automated occasions at each threshold with fp_aggregate(), fits the same model to each, and collects the estimates, so that their sensitivity to the threshold can be seen at once.

Usage

fp_threshold_sweep(
  occasions,
  detections,
  thresholds,
  sites,
  verified = NULL,
  site = "site",
  by = "file",
  species = NULL,
  recorder = NULL,
  occ = ~1,
  det = ~1,
  fp = ~1,
  random_recorder = !is.null(recorder),
  prob = 0.95,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fp_threshold_sweep'
plot(x, parameters = NULL, ...)

Arguments

occasions, detections, by, species

Passed to fp_aggregate().

thresholds

Confidence thresholds to try, for instance those that maximise F1 or precision on a validation set (this function does not derive them).

sites, verified, site, recorder

Passed to fp_data(); site must also be a column of occasions.

occ, det, fp, random_recorder

Passed to fp_occu().

prob

Width of the credible intervals in the summary.

...

Further arguments for fp_occu(), such as chains, threads_per_chain, or seed.

x

An fp_threshold_sweep object.

parameters

Parameters to plot; by default the occupancy slopes and p10_bar.

Value

A data frame of class fp_threshold_sweep with one row per threshold and parameter: the threshold, the share of occasions that are detections, the parameter, its posterior mean and interval, and the number of divergent transitions and largest R-hat of the fit. plot() draws the estimates against the threshold.

References

Piatti, L., de Sousa, D. L. H., Oliveira, B. S., de Melo, A. V., Sugai, L. S. M., & Provete, D. B. (2026). Methodological choices influence ecological inference in passive acoustic monitoring of a Neotropical nightjar. Journal of Avian Biology, in press.

See also

fp_aggregate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# occasions: one row per one-minute recording, with site_night and covariates
sweep <- fp_threshold_sweep(occasions, detections, thresholds = c(0.1, 0.4, 0.7),
                            sites = nights, verified = verified,
                            site = "site_night", occ = ~ temp + rh, fp = ~ 1,
                            random_recorder = FALSE)
plot(sweep)
} # }
